source_refs.note: i. Molecular mass and size:: a main subheading of 5.4.1 Instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces (London dispersion forces), its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 99-99.

blocks.text: When the molecular mass (Mᵣ) of a compound is greater, the id-id forces are stronger and vice versa. This is because in a larger atom or molecule the dispersion of electronic cloud and polarisation is relatively easier. This factor operates in the halogen and noble gas families. The physical state changes in the halogen family from top to bottom due to the increase in size and polarizability. The first two members in the halogen family (F₂ and Cl₂) are gases, but bromine is a liquid and iodine a solid (b.p. = 458 K). The boiling points of noble gases in group 18 also increase from helium (He) to xenon (Xe) as in Table 5.1.
